summary: Correct 46/16 to 45/16.

summary: The nuts example is at 45/16, not 46/16
rationale: 45/16 reads 'Hano, me d marfele ag gawze, xalyo iḏe.', matching the quoted nuts and emptied hand. 45/15 supplies the preceding instruction to release the nuts. The supplied 46/16 instead concerns a third fart and falling dead.

summary: Extract the trapped citation and cite both verses of the dialogue
before: I want you to give me a permission to go and look for her, to bring her” – He said: “My son! We cannot let you go” 74/39;
after: I want you to give me a permission to go and look for her, to bring her” – He said: “My son! We cannot let you go”
rationale: The current translation includes the literal reference 74/39 while refs is empty. The supplied 74/39 contains the request for permission; the father's reply 'Komər: Abri! ... layban marfinalux' is in 74/40. Store the complete range in refs and remove the locator from the translation.

summary: Replace the throwing paraphrase with the edition’s release translation.
before: After he threw out the nuts, his hand became empty
after: Er ließ die Nüsse los, und seine Hand leerte sich.
rationale: The direct edition evidence gives release, not throwing; preserve its German wording.

summary: Correct 'Kopf' to 'Knopf'
rationale: The example concerns a loose button. The supplied Ritter dictionary explicitly glosses rafyo under the same root rpy as 'lose (Knopf)', supporting the missing n in the German noun.

data.translation: »Komm und mache mich los«, rief sie. »Nein, ich mache dich nicht los«. »Wesshalb nicht?« »Wo sind die Augen meines Vaters?« fragte er. »Komm, mache mich los und nimm sie dir«. »Lege sie in meine Hand«, erwiderte er. Sie tat das und bat wieder: »Mache mich los«. »Nein, ich mache dich nicht los«, gab er zur Antwort und ging weg.

rationale: Thin cell; divorce requested from an officiant with couple as patient.

summary: example for sense 6 in Imperativ (PrS 68/94)

data.turoyo: Qralle lu zoġo, əmmi: "Lox mhərilox, arfayən."
data.translation: Da rief man den Hahn und sagte ihm: "Du hast sie getraut; scheide sie nun wieder."

rationale: Thin cell; the officiant who performed marriage is commanded to dissolve it.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (63/107)

data.turoyo: Bəṯr b falga d saʕaye ḥzeli, qarʕe hiz, raġloṯe rafən m aʕli, iḏoṯe hnən, naqqa omər "šalap" w nafəl me ʕal ḥaṣi."
data.translation: Nach einer halben Stunde sah ich, dass sein Kopf schwankte, seine Beine sich lockerten und seine Hände schlaff wurden. Auf einmal fiel er "Bautz!" von meinem Rücken herab.

rationale: Thin I Preterit Intransitive cell; plural rafən plus source m aʕli contrasts with active III.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (115/195)

data.turoyo: Komər, xəd məllale, bəṯr, b saʕaye, taʕibi əšmo, rafən a tre ʕarbayḏe, naqla hama mḥalalqe ruḥe omər: "Ya rab, d ḥozeno, be ma aydarbo gtowe!" Lo kəmmət, a tfaqat d aloho, aloho hawxa kobəʕ, aṯi ʕal ḥaṣe du komo.
data.translation: Nach einer Weile wurden die beiden Widder ein wenig müde, wie sie ihm vorausgesagt hatte, und erschlafften. Da sprang er und dachte: Herrgott, ich will sehen, was werden wird! - Wie es so kam, Gott wollte es so, er kam auf den Rücken des schwarzen.

rationale: Fifth I slackening example: overt animal subject after fatigue, not another loose fastening.

summary: example for sense 7 in Infectum (53/143)

data.turoyo: Qoyəm kmarfe dalolo bi walaye:
data.translation: Er schickt einen Ausrufer in der Stadt herum:

rationale: Previously empty Infectum dispatch cell; retain only the independent crier-sending clause.

summary: example for sense 7 in Infectum (73/208)

data.turoyo: Hawxa ramḥəl marfeno u dalolo bi walaye,
data.translation: Morgen werde ich den Ausrufer in der Stadt herumschicken

rationale: Thin Infectum dispatch cell; first-person unprefixed Infectum with tomorrow.

summary: example for sense 7 in Infectum (101/21)

data.turoyo: Qayəm, mərralle lag gərgər lu ḥakəm, əmmi: “D marfat səḥərdar bi walaye, gməfqo u ḥaramiyano, gməfqo u baṣrano. Bu bayto, tawi, hawo yo u ḥarami.”
data.translation: Nun sprachen die Notabeln zum Wali: Wenn du eine Hexe in der Stadt herumgehen lässest, wird sie diesen Dieb, dieses Fleisch, herausbringen. In dem Hause, wo es ist, da ist der Dieb. -

rationale: Thin dispatch cell; a witch rather than the formulaic herald as sent participant.

summary: example for sense 7 in Imperativ (56/73)

data.turoyo: Əmmi: "Arfewu dalolo bi walaye ṣafro w ṭro qore u dalolo: "Innahu maslamlan ann arbʕi ḥaramiyani lu šerkuž! Kəbʕi, ṭr oṯən masəlmi ruḥayye w lo kəbʕi məṣṭafəl mine w alle!""
data.translation: Die Ratsversammlung sprach: "Schickt Morgen Ausrufer in die Stadt und laßt sie ausrufen: "Wir haben die Sache der vierzig Räuber dem Löwentöter übergeben! Wenn sie wollen, sollen sie sich ihm ergeben, und wenn sie nicht wollen, so mögen sie es mit ihm allein ausmachen!"

rationale: Previously empty Imperativ dispatch cell; m-less Arfewu with explicit herald and route.

summary: example for sense 4 in Infectum-wa (59/88)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d marfanwo aq qarqure qum da ʕwone, u qarqurano u ṣaqaṭ roḥatwo w mṣaʕarwo, omarwo: "Nakno i emo, d noyək emi!"
data.translation: Wenn sie die Lämmer zu den Mutterschafen ließen, sagte dieses Lamm immer: "Ich f ... die Mutter dessen, der meine Mutter f...!"

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa release cell after batch-1 bird correction; overt lamb patient and ewe goal.

summary: example for sense 4 in Infectum-wa (70/184)

data.turoyo: Meqəm u əntəxabaṯṯe d saymiwa, aydarbo wa? Kətwa ṭayro di dawle. Hənna gṭərḏiwa u malko, kətwa u ṭawro di dawle, gmarfənwayle. ʕAl qarʕe d man maḥətle hawo malko.
data.translation: Wie machte man früher die Wahll? Es war da ein Glücksvogel. Wenn sie den König vertreiben wollten, ließen sie den Glücksvogel los. Auf wessen Kopf er sich niederließ, der wurde König.

rationale: Thin Infectum-wa release cell; suffixed singular bird in another election narrative.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (64/309)

data.turoyo: ʕAm u taʕb d taʕəb u zʕurawo aʕma, səmla kayisuṯo aʕme, marfela darmone ba brinatayḏe w manəḥla w hawi saġ.
data.translation: Wegen der Mühe, die der Jungling mit ihr gehabt hatte, tat sie ihm Gutes, tat Heilmittel in seine Wunden, heilte ihn, und er wurde wieder lebending.

rationale: Thin placement cell; medicine in wounds, matching existing leech application.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (65/36)

data.turoyo: Omər marfalle aš šeṯmo kowanaṯṯe li arʕo.
data.translation: Sie schlugen ihre sechs Hundert Zelte auf.

rationale: Thin placement cell; erecting tents with l-ground goal beside existing tent pegs.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit (66/329)

data.turoyo: Hedika mḥalaqqe u šoriṭo li nawqayḏe w marfalle li zarzamiye.
data.translation: Sie warfen ihm unversehens den Strick um die Hüfte und ließen ihn in das unterirdische Gefängnis hinunter.

rationale: Fifth placement example: rope and dungeon make controlled lowering clear.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (66/327)

data.turoyo: Lo tay gmarfinale li zarzamiye, ṭrowe bi zəndanayo hul arbʕi yawme ḥrene gmoṯ mu kafno.
data.translation: Nein komm, wir wollen ihn in das unterirdische Gefängnis hinunterlassen, dann wird er innerhalb von vierzig Tagen hungers sterben.

rationale: Previously empty Infectum placement cell; prospective lowering rather than release from captivity.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (96/45)

data.turoyo: "E", — omər, — "ḥoṯo, balki, aloho yo, hama marfat ṣadrax b feme, balki hama howe ḥalwo b ṣadronax. E la, wa l ḥasəl yo diḏa yo!"
data.translation: Eh, Schwester, vielleicht wird Gott, gib ihm doch mal die Brust, vielleicht entsteht Milch in deinen Brüsten. - Nun, es ist ja ihr Sohn!

rationale: Thin Infectum placement cell; overt breast patient and mouth b-goal.

summary: example for sense 2 in Imperativ (70/218)

data.turoyo: Komər maṣəlle u ḥawlo ʕal ḥaṣe, omər: "Ono məqqa d omanno "grašuli", hatu marfewuli bi biro!"
data.translation: Da band er sich den Strick um und sprach: "Soviel ich auch schreien mag: Zieht mich hoch! Laßt mich in den Brunnen hinunter!"

rationale: Thin Imperativ placement cell; rope-controlled descent into a well; high direction is contrasted in the quoted instruction.

summary: example for sense 8 in Preterit (65/294)

data.turoyo: Omər naḥit lu maydan w afandim annaqqa lar rawixe marfalle ruḥayye, lu maydan aṯən.
data.translation: Er ritt auf den Kampplatz; da strömten die Reiter auf den Kampfplatz und kamen heran.

rationale: Thin reflexive Preterit cell; plural riders and explicit ruḥayye with battlefield goal.

summary: example for sense 8 in Preterit (105/95)

data.turoyo: komər dlo ruḥo marfele ruḥe bad darġe w azzele laf ela.
data.translation: ließ er sich, seiner selbst nicht mächtig, die Treppe hinunter und ging auf sie zu.

rationale: Thin reflexive cell; overt self-patient and stairs, independent of a grave context.

summary: example for sense 8 in Infectum (63/92)

data.turoyo: Gmarfeno ruḥi, d ḥozina, l ayko kəzze u darbano!
data.translation: Ich will mich dem Zufall überlassen; laß uns sehen, wohin dieser Weg führt!

rationale: Thin Infectum self-release cell; explicit reflexive wandering, not a new sense.

summary: example for sense 8 in Infectum (66/103)

data.turoyo: Məlle: "De annaqqa məllalli "maye, maye", gmarfeno ruḥi, lo kowe d marfeno am mayani hul li walaye d Gziro!"
data.translation: Er sprach: "Sie hat mir damals doch gesagt: immer dem Wasser nach! Ich werde immer weiter reiten und dieses Wasser nicht verlassen bis zu der Stadt Gziro."

rationale: Thin Infectum self-release cell; following a river, retaining the source distinction from leaving the river.

summary: example for sense 5b in Imperativ (65/376)

data.turoyo: Izoxu taḥt u kon, arfewu bəhən dəṯxu, məṯneḥu!"
data.translation: geht unter das Zelt, verschnauft euch, ruht euch aus!"

rationale: New Imperativ box for the batch-1 breath-rest subsense; overt breath plus rest command.

summary: example for sense 5b in Imperativ (65/491)

data.turoyo: itaw taḥt u kon, arfi bəhən diḏux, hul d məṯnoḥat w bəṯr itux!
data.translation: setze dich unter das Zelt und verschnaufe dich, bis du dich ausgeruht hast, und dann komm!

rationale: Thin breath-rest Imperativ cell; singular arfi contrasts with plural arfewu.

summary: example for sense 1 in Part. Pass. (69/462)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d kmičək bu ʕafrayḏe, xalaṣ saḥər, kəzze l dukṯe w lo lo, i naqqa d knofəq, marfyo yo.
data.translation: Wenn er nämlich auf dessen Grund und baden kam, wurde er verzaubert und mußte an seinen Platz gehen; wenn aber nicht, wenn er herauskam, war er losgelassen.

rationale: Thin Detransitive free-state cell; masculine predicate marfyo yo contrasts with feminine/plural examples already selected.

summary: example for sense 3 in Imperativ (76/20)

data.turoyo: Omər: "Marfewu dexono bəṯre! U dexono gmaʕəqla aʕle."
data.translation: Der Junge sprach: "Macht Rauch hinter ihm! Der Rauch wird ihn schon in die Enge treiben."

rationale: Thin discharge/release Imperativ cell; smoke theme as substance emission, without a separate fumigation sense.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (61/338)

data.turoyo: I naqqa d marfele, lu sabʕo mḥele danwe b gawe d ruḥe, nafəl gurmen aʕle xəd marfat bəmbaye bi arʕo, hawxa aṯi ḥəs me danwe.
data.translation: Als er nun den Löwen losließ, schlug dieser mit dem Schwanz gegen seinen Bauch, und es gab einen solchen Donner, wie wenn du eine Bombe auf die Erde wirfst; ein solcher Krach ging von seinem Schwanze aus.

rationale: Thin Infectum throwing cell; overt bomb theme and ground goal provide an independent literal comparator.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum (70/207)

data.turoyo: Komər maṭən l fema d biro ʕaməqto, ġalabe ʕaməqto yo. Kmarfən ak kefe eba, koṯe ḥəz dam maye.
data.translation: Sie gelangten an den Rand eines tiefen Brunnens, der war sehr tief. Sie ließen Steine hinunterfallen, da war das Platschen von Wasser zu hören.

rationale: Thin Infectum throwing cell; audible splash confirms stones dropped into a well.

summary: example for sense 3 in Preterit (63/76)

data.turoyo: maḥatli iḏi bayn am maye ste w maḥatli i damančaye ʕal u ḥaywanano w qayəmno, marfeli a šwaʕ ḏ̣arbe ebe.
data.translation: tat ich meine Band ins Wasser, legte die Pistole auf jenes Tier an und feuerte die sieben Schuss auf es ab.

rationale: The nuts correction leaves four cumulative III.3 Preterit examples; add a fifth confirming b-target firearm discharge, without repeating the event at 63/77.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.22/1165)

data.turoyo: Yaʕni di naqqayo d marfenawo, d msalminawo ruḥayna lənne, gəd qəšʕiwolan.
data.translation: That is, at the moment we let go, surrendered ourselves to them, they would have wiped us out.

rationale: Thin III.1 Infectum-wa cell; conditional surrender context, with object left unexpressed.

summary: example for sense 5 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.40/1776)

data.turoyo: ʕAmmo Išoʕ: Yarḥo-tre hul d ubiwo ak kallat dəṯṯe ya ste d məlyowa i məddaṯṯe marfanwonne.
data.translation: Uncle Isho: A month or two, until they paid their money, or else, when their term was filled, they would release them.

rationale: Thin III.5 Infectum-wa cell; explicit payment or expiry endpoint.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.2/125)

data.turoyo: Čaʕ əšne b lalyo w b imomo, mən kṯowo d uṯewo l iḏi, d lə qurenowole naqqa w tarte, hul d lə uḏaʕwowo, mən kibe, lə marfenowole.
data.translation: Nine years, night and day, whatever book came into my hand, I would read it once and twice; until I knew it, what it contained, I would not put it aside.

rationale: Thin III.1 Infectum-wa cell; negative persistence bounded by knowing the contents.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.4/807)

data.turoyo: Bi ḥarayto kul raḥa marfelan i dəkṯayḏan w aṯina, ya Ǧan!
data.translation: In the end, in complete ease, we left our place and came, Jan!

rationale: III.1 Preterit remains thin after round 1; overt first-person plural agent and place object.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (Jan 2.4/1094)

data.turoyo: Xori Brahim: Azzən li dukṯaṯṯe. Rusya marfela i dəkṯaṯṯe w azzən daʕiri li dəkṯaṯṯe.
data.translation: Father Brahim: They went to their own places. Russia left their places and they went back to their places.

rationale: Fills cumulative III.1 Preterit cell up to five; institutional feminine agent Rusya contrasts with preceding human plural.

summary: example for sense 3 in Infectum-wa (Jan 3.54/1523)

data.turoyo: Hawxa mašiġiwo w manḏ̣əfiwaynanne, marfiwayna ste əšmo d malḥo aʕlayye, hiya w ḥarofrofo w i parpare.
data.translation: They would wash them like that, and we cleaned them; we also sprinkled a little salt over them, it and the harofrofo and the purslane.

rationale: Thin III.3 Infectum-wa cell; solid granular scattering beside round-1 fluid discharge.

summary: example for sense 4 in Infectum (Jan 4.II/775)

data.turoyo: yaʕni əno kəmmono i naqqa, emo w babo d lə kmarfəti i barṯo, yaʕni məd kəbʕi… lə kəbʕi yaʕni u medano, mən yo yaʕni?
data.translation: that is, I say, when the mother and father do not release the daughter, that is, because they want… they do not want this, I mean, what is it?

rationale: Unusual written plural marfəti in parental permission; no claim of a new form box.

summary: Move the personal-communication attribution out of the Turoyo field
rationale: The parenthesized personal-communication credit and equals sign are not Turoyo words. The current refs list is empty. Retain the credit as a reference and retain the translation separately.

summary: Sense 3: revise the gloss
after: werfen; (mit Waffen oder Munition als Objekt, auch ohne ausgedrücktes Objekt; Ziel mit ʕal- oder b-) schießen, abfeuern;
rationale: Makes the discharge meaning of the already filed silaḥ/fəšak̇at examples explicit; the new corpus confirms both expressed and omitted objects. Batch 2 (63/76–77) confirms b-targets in firing as well.

summary: Sense 6: revise the gloss
after: scheiden; eine Ehe oder Verlobung auflösen;
rationale: The Turoyo treats spouses or a prospective spouse as the affected participant; the added words extend marital dissolution to the clearly attested betrothal context.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe behən ‘ausatmen’

data.turoyo: W aḥna-ze ṣxəllan behən diḏan, lə=gmaǧrina marfina behən, hul d aṯi me bəṯran-va bəṯr i=kozke, maḥatle ruḥe qəm feme di=tfənge bayn elan w li=mekawe.
data.translation: Und wir hielten den Atem an, wir wagten nicht auszuatmen, bis es hinter uns, hinter dem Ansitz hervorkam und sich vor die Gewehrmündung setzte, zwischen uns und dem weiblichen Steinhuhn.

rationale: New literal breath-release collocation, explicitly opposed to holding breath; lookup behn/bəhn found the existing relaxation example but no exhalation idiom.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe kabrit (mit b-) ‘mit einem Streichholz anzünden’

data.headword: marfele/marfe kabrit (mit b-) ‘mit einem Streichholz anzünden’
data.turoyo: maḥatla tloṯo ṭonat hažžikat aʕla w marfela kabrit biya.
data.translation: sie warf drei Tonnen Zweige darauf und zündete es mit einem Streichholz an.

rationale: Single clear match-object ignition collocation; glossary search kabrit returned no entry. Do not decide between throwing, applying or striking the match.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe ʕayne (mit b-) ‘seine Augen auf jemanden richten’

data.headword: marfele/marfe ʕayne (mit b-) ‘seine Augen auf jemanden richten’
data.turoyo: Marfele ʕayne eba. Marfele ʕayne eba.
data.translation: He cast his eyes on her. He cast his eyes on her.

rationale: New eyes-with-b-target collocation also attested in Dilo and Falako. Full supplied rfy entry has ears but no eyes idiom; no necessary romantic entailment is claimed.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe ḥaṣra ‘einen Seufzer ausstoßen’

data.turoyo: Omər i naqqa d amṭele i dukṯo d Gulbaran l bole, lu zlamano marfele ḥaṣra w kadar rabo.
data.translation: Als er ihm den Ort des Gulbaran in Erinnerung brachte, gab er einen Seufzer von sich und wurde sehr betrübt.

rationale: Single clear emission collocation; glossary search ḥaṣra returned no hit.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe aḥ ḥaye ‘das Leben lassen, sterben’

data.headword: marfele/marfe aḥ ḥaye ‘das Leben lassen, sterben’
data.turoyo: Mʕalaqle u zʕuro w kul saʕaye košəlḥi parčaye me du baṣrayḏe, hul d marfele aḥ ḥaye.
data.translation: Er ließ ihn aufhängen, und alle Stunde riss man ein Stück von seinem Fleische ab, bis er das Leben ließ.

rationale: Life-noun death collocation; lookup ḥaye finds this under ʕlq, but the supplied rfy idioms include only the spirit variant.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe admo (mit m-) ‘Blut aus etwas fließen lassen’

data.headword: marfele/marfe admo (mit m-) ‘Blut aus etwas fließen lassen’
data.turoyo: komər mṭalle aǧ ǧiletkat, komər marfalle admo mi lašayḏe w raysile malḥo, komər hul d mayəṯ.
data.translation: holten Rasierklingen herbei, ließen Blut aus seinem Leibe fließen und streuten Salz in seine Wunden, bis er starb.

rationale: Single clear blood-emission collocation. Supplied rfy has none; search admo does not reveal the phrase in rfy. No healing or medical purpose is inferred.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe u ġar ‘herabstoßen (im Flug)’

data.turoyo: B ġaḏ̣ab w b qaḥər w b məṭalat marfele u ġar, d qoṭele.
data.translation: Zornig, wütend und bekümmert stieß sie herab, um das vermeintliche Untier zu töten.

rationale: Single motion-noun light-verb collocation. Search ġar and the complete supplied rfy entry contain no such item; the gloss stays within this token rather than claiming all running/flight uses.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe ḥaṣ + Poss. ‘jemandem die Unterstützung entziehen’

data.headword: marfele/marfe ḥaṣ + Poss. ‘jemandem die Unterstützung entziehen’
data.turoyo: W marfele ḥaṣayye w msəkke ah Hərməziye kulle mawbələnne qaflat, qaflat w qṭələnne dlo sabab w dlo ḥaq.
data.translation: And he abandoned them, and they seized all the Hirmez people and took them away in convoys, convoy after convoy, and killed them without cause and without right.

rationale: Possessed backs as object, followed by the abandonment of the protected group; one clear attestation. Supplied entry and named round-1 idioms have no such headword.

summary: New idiom: marfele/marfe xabro ‘ein Wort äußern’

data.turoyo: Xabro d marfe d lo fəkər koṯe ṣaqaṭ u xabrawo.
data.translation: A word that he lets out without thinking, that word comes out wrong.

rationale: Word as released content; distinguish from issuing an order without claiming a new numbered sense. No matching headword in entry or round 1.

summary: Existing head, etymology, stem forms, notes and idiom wording are retained. The original senses 1–11 are never renumbered.

Agent coding: Preterit has L-series agents, sometimes doubled by l-NPs; Infectum has person endings and patient suffixes. The performative 29/450 -li is particularly useful against misfiling as Infectum. Do not infer argument role solely from a German/English pronoun.

III.4b is supported across Lahdo and MAC: husk and ash-coating are sole subjects of active III. They contrast with a binder holding stones (transitive III.4) and free-state Part. Pass. predicates (Detransitive). The following separation verb alone governs the overt m-source in Lahdo; do not put obligatory m- in the new gloss.

Aspect: Infectum-wa expresses customary bird release, habitual tending and counterfactual release. Preterit may occur in prospective conditions (PrS 3/14) and as a present act of relinquishment (29/450). These uses do not require changing the glossary box labels.

The existing nuro ignition idiom extends figuratively to distress in the heart (LuF 1/20); fire applied to cannon fuses is still ignition, not III.9 beginning. Existing femo, daqno and aḏno collocations are not proposed anew.

The breath-rest construction is already a numbered use in the team entry; subsense 5b therefore keeps that practice. Literal exhalation is indexed separately as an idiom. A single exhalation attestation suffices because it is explicitly opposed to holding breath.

Routine counts in this input are aggregate evidence: particularly III Preterit 4=70, 5=36; Imperativ 4=32; Infectum 4=32, 1=31, 5=26; marital separation appears in Preterit=9 and Infectum=10. Counts inherit reader assignments and are not independently reclassified or added to batch 2 as fresh totals.

Existing free-state examples have no numbered Detransitive gloss. Detransitive 1/2 labels organise that material; Infinitiv tarfoyo/tərfiyo remains under its inherited Detransitive heading pending editorial review.

Batch 2 is cumulative with batch 1: all earlier sense numbers, examples, idioms, corrections, notes and questions are retained. New direct nuts evidence overrides the previous inherited III.3 assignment; it does not overturn any newly introduced sense number.

The nuts verse supplies a direct citation correction 46/16 → 45/16 and a source-faithful German release translation. The existing Imperativ English throw paraphrase also warrants editorial rechecking against the supplied German command, but no invented edition wording is introduced.
The inherited field availability versus free-state Detransitive distinction remains. 69/544 honor-abandonment has uncertain agreement and is not selected as an example of available property.

terfiyo in 102/66–67 is an action nominal of marital dismissal, fronted before a finite verb or combined with negative existential latla. Its semantic value is clear, but Detransitive sense D1 is not established; the occurrence decisions explicitly withhold that reading.

The cumulative III.3 Preterit cell is reduced by moving the old nuts example to III.4. Further gunfire attestations confirm the b-target frame; no indiscriminate filling with repeated shots is required. Controlled lowering is grouped with III.2.

The physiological and idiomatic breath expressions remain separate from dying: possessed breath plus resting is 5b; life/spirit relinquishment expresses death. Causative exhalation is already indexed as a batch-1 idiom.

Routine counts in the batch metadata duplicate the aggregate snapshot from batch 1; they are not summed as independent observations. Exactly 71 full-token decisions are supplied here, in addition to the 150 in batch 1.

All 91 input records receive a decision, including compact records. Compact records lack source verses and cannot be independently checked; no examples are taken from them. routine_counts are not added as new token decisions.
Round 1 already filled III.5 Preterit, III.6 Preterit and Infectum, III.4 Infectum and much Imperativ material. Reader claims of empty cells use the unrevised glossary snapshot and are not followed.

Preterit-wa is already a round-1 box; Jan supplies new sense cells 5 and 6, not a new box. marfiyowale has a possible pre-agent feminine object; the parallel divorce predicate supports the event meaning without settling suffix segmentation.

The intercessor dayroyo as releasing agent permits indirect agency. Institutional Rusya and maḥkame are ordinary active agents, not Detransitive subjects. marfela contains an agent -la, not merely an object -la.
Repeated book-reading scenes are consistently grouped under putting aside (III.1). Fire, spirit/death and blood phrases already have idiom coverage; they are not new numbered senses.
The Jan collection here includes interview dialogue and vernacular code-switching as well as written prose; no uniformly learned-register behavior is inferred.
Source English is supplied machine translation. The reader reports a role reversal at Jan 2.4/715; its English is not quoted. Meaning and agent analysis remain based on the Turoyo.
Confirm the contracted forms marfewola (Preterit-wa), marfela, marfalalle, kmarfatte, arfayli/arfili/arfawulli, and the object/recipient segmentation; the source spellings are retained.

summary: Slackness extends to an arm, a facial expression, a government and the gradual easing of conflict. The subject changes; no separate tension/government meaning is needed.
A plot can be left open to livestock; grazing specifies use of available land. Retained vine shoots and permission for young animals to suck show contextual specialisations.

Themes include water and venom; directed release is already represented by the inherited swamp-water example. A sword stroke is compatible with forceful delivery but is not independently established as a technical subsense.
Release applies to buckets, adhering building material, trap mechanisms and attached body parts or hair. The trap can close as a result; release does not entail freedom of a sentient patient.
Self-withdrawal can lack overt ruḥo. PrS 18/9 is compatible with an understood self-patient; MAC Mor Barsaumo/38 remains ambiguous between bodily relaxation and stopping prayer.

Honor and the good/bad in advice are abstract objects that can be relinquished; no fixed honor idiom is established by a single noun. Illness may be the active subject that leaves/releases its sufferer, not a Detransitive patient.
A body part can be placed on a saddle or in a child’s mouth; a rope permits controlled lowering with a dungeon/well goal. Direction and participant alone do not require a separate sense.
A person softens resistance on seeing money; this supports the round-1 abstract relaxation extension rather than a new sense.
Controlled lowering includes waste into a pit and a wick into a wax pan, continuing round-1 lowering with a goal. No independent carry sense is established by Jan 2.3/358.
Two ʕal-goals describe property joined to a courtyard or barracks. The accompanying attachment verb supports integration, but legal annexation versus opening the site remains unresolved.

The round-1 marfe admo blood-emission idiom now has an annual therapeutic regimen, with the treated person apparently serving as the releasing agent. This is a medical application of the existing collocation, not a repeated idiom proposal.
